items.title: Sheila Jordan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Middleburgh, New York, May 11, 2002
items.q: once Duke and I got married

ctx.x: Was that, did you ever have any similar incidents with your marriage like that?

Uhh. No, and I’ll tell you why. Because once Duke and I got married, we weren’t together very long. It was weird. We actually were together a total of seven years, but up until the time after my daughter was born, shortly after my daughter was born, I was just too much for him and he had his own personal problems which I won’t go into detail, and he left. And you know, now that I think back about it, it was the best thing that ever happened to me. He did me the biggest favor in life. Because trying to deal with…

this music, I was. That’s why today if it’s like the reverse prejudice now, against white musicians among some of the younger musicians coming up, some of the younger Afro- American musicians coming up, I think oh my God if you only knew how much I suffered to keep this music alive. Whether it’s singing it, spreading the word, going to the clubs, teaching it, whatever. You have no idea how hard I worked.
